exEn: I'm wearing a white blouse.
note: Diminutive of 'camicia' (shirt).

exEn: In winter I put on my beanie.
note: 'Cappello' is a hat with a brim; 'berretto' is a soft cap.

exEn: I have wool socks on.
note: 'Calze' = socks/stockings/tights; 'calzini' = short socks.

ex: Per la festa metto un abito elegante.
exEn: For the party I'll wear an elegant dress.
note: 'Gli abiti' = clothes in general. 'Abito da sera' = evening dress.

exEn: This top is made of cotton.
note: Generic word for a knitted or jersey top; 'maglione' = heavy sweater, 'maglietta' = T-shirt.

exEn: The shirt is missing a button.
At home I wear slippers.
I have the keys in my pocket.
note: Plural with h: tasche.

exEn: My mother has a lot of jewellery.

ex: Al mare porto gli occhiali da sole.
exEn: At the seaside I wear sunglasses.
note: Plural noun, like 'occhiali'.

exEn: The film is very funny.
My sister is very intelligent.
What a silly question!
note: Quite strong when said of a person; 'sciocco' is milder.

exEn: Marco is very sporty.
note: 'Abbigliamento sportivo' = sportswear / casual clothes.

exEn: Stay calm, everything is fine.
note: 'Calma!' as an exclamation = calm down! Also of the sea: il mare è calmo.

exEn: I have a surprise for you!
note: 'Che sorpresa!' = what a surprise!; 'a sorpresa' = surprise (party).

ex: Sei fortunato, hai una bella famiglia.
exEn: You're lucky, you have a lovely family.
note: Opposite: sfortunato.

exEn: Anna has a nice smile.
I feel like an ice cream.
note: 'Avere voglia di' + noun/infinitive = to feel like. 'Non ho voglia' = I don't feel like it.

ex: Che emozione, il primo giorno di scuola!
exEn: How exciting, the first day of school!
With Luca we have lots of laughs.
note: 'Farsi una risata' = to have a laugh.

exEn: In the mountains we make a fire.
note: Plural with h: fuochi. 'Fuochi d'artificio' = fireworks; 'vigili del fuoco' = firefighters.

ex: Il libro è caduto per terra.
exEn: The book fell on the ground.
note: 'Per terra' = on the ground/floor. Capitalised 'la Terra' = the planet Earth.

exEn: Do you want ice in your water?
note: 'Con ghiaccio' / 'senza ghiaccio' when ordering drinks.

ex: Che tempo fa oggi a Milano?
exEn: What's the weather like in Milan today?
note: Answers use 'fa' (fa caldo, fa freddo, fa bel tempo) or 'c'è' (c'è il sole, c'è vento).

exEn: It's very hot today.
note: Weather uses 'fare'; for people use 'avere': ho caldo = I'm hot.

exEn: In January it's cold.
note: For people: ho freddo = I'm cold.

exEn: Milan is in the north of Italy.
note: 'Al nord' / 'a nord di' = in the north / north of.

exEn: Naples is in the south.
note: 'Il Sud' (capitalised) often means southern Italy, il Mezzogiorno.

ex: Venezia è a est di Milano.
exEn: Venice is east of Milan.

ex: Torino è a ovest di Milano.
exEn: Turin is west of Milan.
The weather is nice today.
note: Also 'fa bel tempo'. 'Bel' is the form of 'bello' before a masculine noun starting with a consonant.

ex: Con il brutto tempo resto a casa.
exEn: In bad weather I stay at home.
note: Also 'fa brutto tempo' / 'fa brutto'.

ex: Oggi c'è il sole, andiamo al mare!
exEn: It's sunny today, let's go to the seaside!
It's windy, take your jacket.
note: Also 'tira vento'.

exEn: The Italian alphabet has twenty-one letters.
note: J, K, W, X and Y are used only in foreign words.

ex: Scrivo una lettera a mia nonna.
exEn: I'm writing a letter to my grandmother.
Repeat the sentence, please.
Can I ask a question?
note: 'Fare una domanda' = to ask a question (not 'chiedere una domanda').

exEn: The answer is correct.

ex: Aprite il libro a pagina dieci.
exEn: Open your books at page ten.
I look the word up in the dictionary.

ex: Il mio banco è vicino alla finestra.
exEn: My desk is near the window.
note: Plural with h: banchi. Also the counter in a bar: 'al banco' = at the counter.

exEn: The classroom is big and bright.

ex: Prendete un foglio e una penna.
exEn: Take a sheet of paper and a pen.
Quiet, please!

ex: Ho bisogno di un foglio di carta.
exEn: I need a sheet of paper.
note: Also: carta d'identità (ID card), carta di credito, giocare a carte (to play cards), carta geografica (map).

exEn: How do you say "dog" in Italian?
note: Impersonal 'si' = one / you in general.

exEn: What does "gatto" mean?
note: 'Voler dire' = to mean; also 'cosa significa?'

en: how do you spell it?; how is it written?
ex: Come si scrive il tuo nome?
exEn: How do you spell your name?
Sorry, could you repeat that?
note: Informal: 'puoi ripetere?'

ex: Non capisco, parla più piano per favore.
exEn: I don't understand, speak more slowly please.
note: Past: 'non ho capito' = I didn't understand.

exEn: Professor, I have a question.
The translation is easy.
The pharmacist is very kind.
note: Same form for both genders; plural farmacisti / farmaciste.

ex: Il tassista conosce bene la città.
exEn: The taxi driver knows the city well.
note: Plural tassisti / tassiste.

exEn: My uncle is a pilot.
note: Same form for both genders. No article after 'essere' with professions: è pilota.

ex: La barista fa un buon cappuccino.
exEn: The barista makes a good cappuccino.
note: Plural baristi / bariste.

exEn: The pizza maker works in the evening.
The baker opens at six.
note: Also 'fornaio'.

exEn: My mother is a housewife.
note: Plural with h: casalinghe. The masculine 'casalingo' is rare and also means 'home-made' as an adjective.

exEn: My grandfather is retired.
note: 'Essere in pensione' = to be retired.

exEn: I'm taking the cat to the vet.
note: 'Dal veterinario' = to/at the vet's (da + person).

ex: Il fotografo fa una foto alla famiglia.
exEn: The photographer takes a photo of the family.
The postman comes at ten.
The firefighters arrive right away.
note: Official term: 'vigile del fuoco'. Emergency number: 115.

exEn: My brother is a musician.
note: Plural musicisti / musiciste.

en: what do you do (for a living)?
exEn: What do you do? I'm a teacher.
note: Formal: 'che lavoro fa?'. Answer with 'sono' / 'faccio il/la' + job.

exEn: The electrician is coming tomorrow.
The tiger lives in Asia.
note: Feminine noun used for both male and female animals.

ex: La giraffa ha il collo lungo.
exEn: The giraffe has a long neck.
The ducks are swimming in the lake.
On Sunday we're going to the zoo.
note: Invariable; note 'allo zoo' (a + lo).

exEn: The rooster crows in the morning.
The crocodile lives in the river.

ex: Il canguro è un animale australiano.
exEn: The kangaroo is an Australian animal.
Penguins love the cold.

ex: La zebra è bianca e nera.
exEn: The zebra is black and white.
note: 'Le strisce (zebre)' colloquially = zebra crossing.

ex: In estate i girasoli sono gialli.
exEn: In summer the sunflowers are yellow.
note: Literally 'turns to the sun'.

ex: Ho mangiato troppo e ho mal di pancia.
exEn: I ate too much and I have a stomach ache.
note: 'Avere mal di' + body part, without article.

ex: Ho mal di gola e non parlo bene.
exEn: I have a sore throat and I can't speak well.

ex: Ho mal di denti, vado dal dentista.
exEn: I have toothache, I'm going to the dentist.

ex: Mio padre ha spesso mal di schiena.
exEn: My father often has back pain.

ex: Compro lo spazzolino e il dentifricio.
exEn: I'm buying a toothbrush and toothpaste.
I'm on a diet, no sweets.
note: 'Essere a dieta' = to be on a diet.

exEn: I feel weak today.
note: Opposite: forte.

exEn: I take a pill after lunch.
note: Also 'pastiglia' / 'compressa' (tablet).

exEn: Do you have an aspirin?
The shampoo has run out.
note: Note the article 'lo' before s + consonant.

exEn: There's no more toilet paper.
I put cream on my hands.
note: 'Crema solare' = sun cream. Also a custard-style cream in desserts.
